title: Residue-fibre regular initial forms lift through a flat associated graded ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal, set $A=R/I$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/I$, $k=R/\mathfrak m$, and put $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}G_j$ with $G_j=I^j/I^{j+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Assume $G$ is flat over $A$, meaning that tensoring any injection of $A$-modules with $G$ preserves injectivity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then every $G_j$ is finite free over $A$. Write $F=G\otimes_Ak$. For every $n\ge0$ and $a\in I^n$, let $\alpha=a\bmod I^{n+1}\in G_n$ and $h=\alpha\otimes1\in F_n$. If multiplication by $h$ is injective on $F$, then multiplication by $\alpha$ gives an injective map $G_j\to G_{j+n}$ for every $j\ge0$, and $a$ is a nonzerodivisor of $R$: $ab=0$ implies $b=0$ for every $b\in R$. No reducedness or characteristic hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: First $A=R/I$ is Noetherian and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/I$: ideals of $A$ are inverse images of ideals of $R$ containing $I$, so their generators descend, and maximal ideals correspond to maximal ideals of $R$ containing $I$. Fix $j$. Since $R$ is Noetherian, $I^j$ has finitely many generators $x_1,\ldots,x_t$. Their classes generate $G_j=I^j/I^{j+1}$ over $A$: reduce coefficients in an expression $x=\sum r_ix_i$ modulo $I$, since $I I^j=I^{j+1}$. Thus $G_j$ is finite over $A$, including $j=0$.

source.place: Elementary quotient-ideal correspondence and the definition of Noetherian; finite graded-piece argument supporting Tag 00NZ (lemma-finite-flat-local).

proof.text: Let $i_j:G_j\to G$ and $p_j:G\to G_j$ be the homogeneous inclusion and projection, with $p_ji_j=1$. For an injection $v:U\to V$ of $A$-modules and $z\in U\otimes_A G_j$ with $(v\otimes1)z=0$, its image $(1\otimes i_j)z$ is killed by $v\otimes1_G$, hence vanishes by the assumed flatness of $G$. Applying $1\otimes p_j$ gives $z=0$. Tensor functoriality therefore proves flatness of $G_j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] over the local ring $A$ to obtain freeness. This is finite freeness: a basis of a finitely generated free module is finite, since the union of the finite basis supports of a finite generating set must contain every basis vector.

source.place: Tag 00NZ (lemma-finite-flat-local), applied after the explicit direct-summand argument.

proof.text: Fix $n,a,\alpha,h$ as in the statement. Write $\mu_j:G_j\to G_{j+n}$ for multiplication by $\alpha$. For every $A$-module $M$ the map $M\otimes_A k\to M/\mathfrak nM$, $x\otimes\bar c\mapsto cx\bmod\mathfrak nM$, is well defined by bilinearity, independently of the lift $c\in A$; its inverse sends $[x]$ to $x\otimes1$. The inverse kills $\mathfrak nM$ since $\mathfrak n k=0$, and the two composites are identities on classes and pure tensors. These formulas also show naturality for $\mu_j$. The map $G_j\otimes_Ak\to F$ induced by $i_j$ has left inverse induced by $p_j$. Multiplication by $h$ on its image is the map induced by $\mu_j$, followed by the inclusion $G_{j+n}\otimes_Ak\to F$, as one checks on pure tensors using the graded multiplication formula. Thus injectivity of multiplication by $h$ on $F$ implies injectivity of $\mu_j\otimes_Ak$, or equivalently of $G_j/\mathfrak nG_j\to G_{j+n}/\mathfrak nG_{j+n}$.

source.place: Elementary tensor/quotient identification by the displayed inverse maps; fibre map in Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-mod-injective] to the identity local homomorphism $A\to A$, with its source module $N=G_j$, target module $M=G_{j+n}$, and $u=\mu_j$. Step 1 supplies Noetherianity of the target ring $A$ and finiteness of $N$; step 2 supplies flatness of $M$; step 3 supplies injectivity modulo the maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. Its conclusion gives injectivity of $\mu_j$ for every $j\ge0$. The additional flat-cokernel conclusion is not needed.

source.place: Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective), injectivity conclusion for the identity local ring homomorphism.

proof.text: Let $b\in R$ satisfy $ab=0$. Inductively prove $b\in I^j$ for all $j\ge0$. The base case is $I^0=R$. If $b\in I^j$, its class $\beta=b\bmod I^{j+1}\in G_j$ satisfies $\alpha\beta=ab\bmod I^{n+j+1}=0$ by the defining homogeneous multiplication. Step 4 implies $\beta=0$, so $b\in I^{j+1}$. This establishes the induction also when $n=0$.

source.place: Elementary induction using the homogeneous multiplication formula, after the Tag 00ME application.

proof.text: The unique maximal ideal of the local ring $R$ is its Jacobson radical, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ is contained in that radical. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] to the Noetherian ring $R$, the ideal $I$, and the cyclic finite module $R$: $\bigcap_{j\ge0}I^jR=0$. Step 5 places $b$ in this intersection, hence $b=0$. This proves the nonzerodivisor conclusion without any reducedness or characteristic assumption.

lean.statement: theorem flat_graded_fibre_regular_lift {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) [Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (associatedGraded I)] : (∀ j : ℕ, ∃ (r : ℕ) (v : Fin r → associatedGradedPiece I j), ∀ x : associatedGradedPiece I j, ∃! c : Fin r → (R ⧸ I), (∑ i : Fin r, c i • DirectSum.of (associatedGradedPiece I) j (v i)) = DirectSum.of (associatedGradedPiece I) j x) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (a : (I ^ n : Ideal R)), Function.Injective (associatedGradedFibreMul I (Ideal.Quotient.factor hI) n a) → (∀ j : ℕ, Function.Injective (associatedGradedMul I n j (Submodule.Quotient.mk a))) ∧ ∀ b : R, a.val * b = 0 → b = 0)
